gen-fs-new-title-gf-david-libre: David Libre reads dignified and refined, its terminals hanging open on a moderate-height lowercase that feels settled and traditional. New Title is the showman, tall and tightly linked; David Libre is the one that holds steady.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-enriqueta: Tall lowercase letters locked together like links in a fine chain give New Title its bold, modern look up top. Enriqueta follows with literary curves that stop short of closing.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-fenix: Fenix reads like a classic serif with an editorial streak, its curved strokes ending before they turn inward. New Title sits above it, tall and bold, in a clear step up.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-gentium-plus: Tall, chain-linked and bold, New Title makes its entrance quickly. Gentium Plus takes over with a refined text serif, each c opening wide like the mouth of a pitcher, at a more moderate lowercase height.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-gowun-batang: Literary and refined, Gowun Batang cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap in each letter. And New Title answers above it, bold and modern, with tall lowercase letters linked tightly like a fine chain.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-habibi: Traditional in spirit, Habibi leads each round letter in through a clear channel. Because its lowercase is only moderate in height, it can take a little more size than you might expect, while New Title stays bold and tall.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-inika: Tall lowercase letters, locked together like links in a fine chain, mark New Title as bold and modern. It makes the statement while Inika, a text serif with a see-through gap in each s, does the quieter work of carrying the words.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-kay-pho-du: New Title is bold and modern, its tall lowercase linked together like a fine chain. But Kay Pho Du, a serif with counters that breathe like a cut reed, would read in a traditional, steady, single-width line over a longer passage.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-labrada: Labrada is dignified and bookish, with wide openings on small letters. New Title brings tall, bold, chain-linked lowercase on top, and the text serif below it sits lower and more moderate, giving the page two clear levels.
